name: Custify App
description:
This is the documentation for APIs from the Custify App. # INTRODUCTION The Custify API is a RESTful API. The requests and responses are formatted according to the JSON API specification. It might happen that you requested to run your Custify application within a data center that's optimized for your location. In this case, you might have to use a different API endpoint URL, instead of https://api.custify.com, to optimize your calls. You'll find your API URL within the app at [Settings -> Developers -> API Key](https://app.custify.com/settings/developer/api-key). ### Data imports In general, there are 3 ways to synchronize your customer data and their events with Custify *on an ongoing basis*: - The Custify API - The Custify JavaScript snippet - An available integration with one of your systems (e.g., via Segment.com) This documentation covers the Custify API and JavaScript snippet. Individual integrations are documented separately. For the *initial* data import, you have several options: - Write a script that uses the Custify API to run through your customers and call the API for each one of them - An available integration into one of your systems that pulls the customer data from there (e.g., Hubspot) ### Data types The data type of the first submission (import or API request) defines the data type of an attribute or event metadata within Custify (Boolean, Integer, Date, or String). We'll try to auto-detect the type of the attribute (or event metadata) in the following order: Date, Number and Boolean. If none of these types will match the type of the attribute will be set to String. For an attribute or event metadata to be detected as Date it should be sent in the following ISO 8601 formats: `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss`, `YYYY-MM-DD`, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss`, `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm`, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSS`, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ`, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ` or `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSSSSZ`. Otherwise, they'll be treated as Strings. These attributes must be sent as UTC dates or using the timezone format. Example: ```json { "company_id": "25", "custom_attributes": { "date": "2020-09-25T10:00:00", "date_format": "2020-09-25T10:00:00.000" } } ``` For an attribute (or event metadata) to be detected as a Number you could send it as in the following example: ```json { "company_id": "25", "custom_attributes": { "team_mates": 5, "team_mates_number": "7", "also_number": 10.2, "other_number": "5.4" } } ``` For an attribute (or event metadata) to be detected as a Boolean you could send it as in the following example: ```json { "company_id": "25", "custom_attributes": { "unsubscribed": true, "unsubscribed_false": "FALSE" "unsubscribed_true": "true" } } ``` This initial data type is later used to compare attributes of different entities (e.g., when creating segments or searching). Although you can send a different data type later on, the first submission defines the data type that Custify uses for this field. We highly recommend never switching the data type for your custom attributes. If you need to change it, submit a new attribute for all customers with the new data type. You can also set values to null. You might do this, for example, if you no longer have a valid value for one of your attributes. ### Rate limiting The API may limit the submission of requests for your application. The limits are managed as an allowed number of operations per time window; an operation might be a read or an update. If you're not on a special enterprise plan, API calls are limited to `100 requests` per `10 seconds` time window. If the limit is reached, a `429 Too Many Requests` response code will be returned along with the following headers: #### Rate limit headers: - `X-RateLimit-Limit`: Maximum number of operations allowed in the current window - `X-RateLimit-Remaining`: Number of operations left in the current window. - `Retry-After`: Number of seconds starting from the first request in the window after the rate limit window will be reset. Further limitations on certain objects (like the maximum length of strings, range of integers) are documented in the individual API calls. ### Postman collection Postman is a tool that lets you build and test HTTP requests in an easy-to-use interface without configuring a full development environment. The Custify Postman Collection is a set of preconfigured requests that make it possible to get started with the Custify API from Postman without having to manually configure the requests. You can download the collection from here => (POSTMAN collection). To use the collection you can create a new environment (let's say `Custify`) and create the 2 needed variables `ApiUrl` and `ApiKey` which are available here [Settings -> Developers -> API Key](https://app.custify.com/settings/developer/api-key). # AUTHENTICATION ### API When you sign up for an account, you're given your account ID. This ID is visible within [Settings -> Developers -> API Key](https://app.custify.com/settings/developer/api-key). *Never share the API key and only use the API key for API calls, not for JavaScript calls*. Keep it guarded and secure, *as anyone with this key will have full read and write access to your data*. You authenticate to the Custify API by providing your API key in the request header (`Authorization: Bearer `). ### JavaScript snippet When you sign up for an account, you're given your account ID. This ID will be visible to you within the Settings -> Developer section. # JAVASCRIPT We offer an easy and fast integration via a JavaScript snippet, a block of code you can insert in pages of your app. It's a fast way to send data to the Custify app and the ideal way to track events like clicked buttons or menu items and/or to track time spent in your product. ## Send data using the JavaScript snippet The JavaScript snippet is a low-impact way to send data to [api.custify.com](https://api.custify.com). While an API integration is more flexible, this is a quick way to get started. ### How to use the JavaScript snippet to send data #### Step 1: Add the basic JavaScript On every page that you want to track events (e.g., button clicks) or to track the time spent in the product, include the script found at [Settings -> Developers -> JS snippet](https://app.custify.com/settings/developer/js-snippet) just before the closing tag. #### Step 2: Identify your account and the user Every event within your application (e.g., “button clicked” or “login”) or the time spent in product is generated from a specific user. For Custify to know which of the users it should attribute the event(s) to, you need to specify the user with an ID and/or email address before sending an event. If the user is part of one or more companies you can link the event to a specific company using the attribute company_id. This attribute is optional. - The user ID is referenced in the code below as `USER_ID` and represents the unique ID of the user *within your systems/CRMs*. It's part of the API call to create that user in the first place. - The email is referenced as `USER_EMAIL` and represents the unique email of the user within your systems/CRMs. - The company is referenced as `COMPANY_ID` and represents the unique ID of the company within your systems/CRMs. For the identification of the account and user, you need to add the identification function to your code *beneath the aforementioned basic Javascript*: ```javascript ``` Custify recommends that you use both userID and email to ensure that users can be identified correctly. The user must already exist in your Custify application before you send events through the JavaScript snippet. #### Step 3: Track events Simple page view tracking can be done by the following snippet: ```javascript ``` Event tracking (i.e., after a button click) can be done using the following snippets as examples: *pure Javascript* ```html ``` *using jQuery* ```javascript ``` *The second parameter of the `track` function should be a JSON object carrying the additional metadata for that specific event*. One possible example for a tracked event would be this: ```javascript _ctrack.track("Checkout complete", { "Item1": "4$", "Item2": "7$"}); ``` #### Step 4: Track time spent in your product Tracking the time spent on a page can be done using the following snippet: ```javascript ``` where `module` represents the name you give to that specific page. The time in product for a user is tracked if one of the actions is detected: mouse move, click, scroll or keyboard input. If in the default idle time of `60` seconds no action is detected the tracking of time is stopped. The default idle time can be changed by adding a new field in the JSON object for the `trackTime` function: ```javascript ``` On pages that you don't want to track the time don't include the function `trackTime`. If your application is a SPA (single-page application) and you don't want to track a specific page you'll have to stop the tracking using the function `stopTrackTime`: ```javascript ``` #### Step 5: Create or update people / companies In order to be able to the create/update people and/or companies through the JS snippet 2 different options have to be turned on: - one is from within the app at [Settings -> Developers -> JS snippet](https://app.custify.com/settings/developer/js-snippet) where you have to toggle ON the setting `Allow creating/updating people and companies via the JS snippet`, otherwise calls will be rejected with a HTTP 403 Forbidden code - one in the JS snippet code where you need to set the `createOrUpdateEntities` to `true` via the `setOptions` method **before** doing the `identify` call ```javascript ``` In order to send entities to Custify, you need to amend the `_ctrack.identify()` call as it follows - adding the 2nd parameter to the call, where you include the entity attributes: ``` _ctrack.identify( { userId: 'USER_ID', // Your Id of the user email: 'USER_EMAIL', // Email of the user company_id: 'COMPANY_ID' // Your Id of the company }, { // The People entity within Custify user: { name: "John Doe", email: 'john.doe@example.com', //if provided will overwrite the one on top, if not we use the one on top unsubscribed_from_emails: false, //example of default attribute custom_attributes: { //an object of custom_attributes, as described in the People Creation API attr_1: "test", attr_2: 123, ... } }, // The Company entity within Custify company: { name: "ACME Corporation", monthly_revenue: 10000, custom_attributes: { has_employees: false, employees_number: 0, owner: "Road Runner", ... } } } ); ``` If a `company` entity will be sent, then a Company record will be created or updated, depending on the `company_id` provided. If a `user` entity will be sent, then a People record will be created or updated, depending on the `user_id` provided. If there is a `user` entity sent and also a `company_id` specified in the first parameter of the identify call, then the user will be linked to that company (if it exists), no matter if a `company` entity is also provided or not. #### Step 6: Trigger in-app survey In order to be able to trigger a in-app survey in your application through the JS snippet following things must happen: - update/install your JS snippet code to the latest version so that you can call the new functions `triggerPendingAction` and `closePendingAction` like in [Settings -> Developers -> JS snippet](https://app.custify.com/settings/developer/js-snippet) - request your CSM to get activated this option - after this option is activated for your account you can define a playbook that triggers the in-app survey step for certain companies/people - on the pages where you want to display the in-app survey, just trigger the `triggerPendingAction` function of the JS Snippet as such `_ctrack.triggerPendingAction()`, which will check the Custify backend for any actions available for the previously identified user (and company) that were set through the `_ctrack.idenfify()` call. Can be triggered on a page load or on a button click (or any valid action). - the HTML code of the in-app area has the following structure, but the exact styles (which are added inline) depend on the settings made in the Playbook step (where you can select the survey placement, the number of times it will be displayed and the number of days the survey will be available): ```
Close
``` - if you want, you can further customize the look, feel and placement of the survey using the CSS classes provided, but for some properties using `!important` might be required.
